constraints: Inference-core (Rust) owns the chain; the Go failover package in capability-core is an inert contract and the wrong plane for runtime state. Master ownership matrix rule 17 says enforcers honour a ZDR waiver only for the exact connection named and "never re-route"; fallback.rs tests assert a subscription outage never reaches an API provider and a ZDR turn pinned to the subscription never lands on Azure; the parity audit records "none on the subscription route by design". Every hop must keep passing ZDR, privacy-tier, residency and budget gates, and health probes must carry no user content and be metered. Config registers one key per provider today, so a credential pool has nothing to rotate until multiple keys or deployments per provider exist.
approachAdjustment: Keep only: a closed failure enum, per-(provider, model) cooldown and benching with reset_at in fallback.rs for API providers, and a health/availability field on ModelInfo surfaced in /v1/models and the picker. Remove the automatic usage-limit fallback and switch-back from the subscription route; if the owner wants continuity, offer an explicit per-turn "continue on a platform model" action with its own consent and ZDR/waiver check, never a silent reroute. Defer credential pools until multi-key config exists, and defer refusal fallback until adapters emit a typed refusal signal.
effortNote: Original L bundled credential pools, subscription fallback with switch-back and refusal rerouting. The keepable core (failure enum, cooldown/bench, health on ModelInfo and picker) is M.
verdictReason: The base chain, typed throttling and typed subscription refusals exist, and the rest is absent, so the item stands. But the subscription fallback and switch-back clash with rule 17 and the by-design no-failover decision, and the credential-pool part has no multi-key baseline, so the item must be narrowed.

exactGap: capability-core EvaluateCapability (engine.go) decides per capability id from a risk heuristic plus the org scope-grant table, EvaluatePolicyRequest carries no target or arguments, and execution-core permission::evaluate_call checks arguments only against fixed keyword lists; hook rules are tool-name globs, first-match-wins, fail-open and held in an in-memory HookRegistry. So there is no durable user or admin rule set over typed targets, no ask-session level, no strictest-wins merge and no CEL dependency. There is also no MCP gate, because both loops refuse MCP tools until capability-core issues a durable binding.
reuse: capability-core policy Engine and its signed Allow evidence (execution-core already verifies it and fails closed for unbound tools)
The execution-core hook matcher and the HookRegistry to hook_context_json wire, as the pattern for delivering rules to a run
permission::evaluate_call, which already receives tool_input, as the place to derive a server-side target

constraints: capability-core IsSupportedScope accepts only org and global; agent, run, thread, workspace and user scopes are rejected until trusted identity bindings exist, so thread, user and Space rules cannot be evaluated in EvaluatePolicy yet. Owner-plane effects and consent-to-disclose tools are never auto-approved (permission/mod.rs), and ownership matrix rule 12 keeps provider writes behind a per-effect signed authorisation, so an allow rule can never relax those. Targets (domain, recipient) must be derived by execution-core from validated arguments, never taken from model text. Space-scoped rules may narrow but must not widen an owner-plane ACL.
approachAdjustment: First cut: add a server-derived typed target to EvaluatePolicyRequest (proto change in Go and Rust) and a durable rule table in capability-core (not the in-memory hook registry), org scope only, admin-authored and audited, resolved strictest-wins. Thread, user and Space "don't ask again" rules wait for F-t3-006 trusted bindings; until then keep them as per-run grants only. Treat CEL as a separate later increment, and add the MCP receipt gate only after F-t3-003 gives per-tool capability ids. Drop the claim about nine quarantined capabilities, which I did not verify.
effortNote: Unchanged: proto change, durable store, strictest-wins resolver and a settings page span three services plus the SPA; CEL and MCP receipts come on top.
verdictReason: Editable rules are genuinely absent (the Space approval panel and the chat design doc both record that no standing answer exists), but the proposed Space, user and thread scopes are not evaluable by capability-core today and the target must be a new proto field, so the approach needs rewording before it can be built.

verdictReason: The item is not absent: part of the speed-tier mechanism is live behind the Quick mode, so its gap statement (no user-facing speed control) is wrong. The rest is real and unbuilt.

exactGap: Single-file HTML artifacts render in a sandbox=allow-scripts iframe (no same-origin, no-network CSP); ArtifactKind has only code, document, html, spreadsheet, file and image with one text content string capped at 200,000 characters, so there is no multi-file bundle kind. The Space sandbox (process_start, code_interpreter) has no network, runs python or sh only and exposes no port, so there is no build step, no per-run preview origin and no screenshot-of-preview loop (screenshot_ref exists only on Quarry browser observations).

constraints: The preview CSP allows only inline script and style plus data: and blob: images and media, so blob: script URLs, external scripts and ES module imports would be blocked: a bundle must be inlined into one srcdoc or the CSP and origin model changed deliberately. allow-same-origin must stay out of the sandbox. A per-run preview origin needs strict CSP and no cookies. Quarry decides whether it may navigate to that origin (the Model proposes, Quarry executes), so the origin must be allow-listed with Quarry, never opened from a Model Plane browser. ZDR runs must not persist builds past the sandbox lease. The process tools need an entitled Space with the space:processes lease claim, and the sandbox has no node toolchain or network today.
approachAdjustment: Phase 0 should inline all bundle files into one srcdoc at render time (still no same-origin and the same CSP) rather than use blob URLs, and should reject module imports between files. Keep phases 1 and 2 behind F-t3-009 and F-t3-045; do not promise a build until a pre-baked toolchain image exists.
effortNote: Unchanged as a whole; Phase 0 alone (bundle kind, tool schema, SPA inlining) is M and can ship independently, while phase 1 is closer to XL because it needs the pre-baked toolchain and a served origin.
verdictReason: The multi-file, build and preview parts are absent and the single-file foundation is exactly as described; only the Phase 0 mechanism needs the CSP correction.

exactGap: The MCP baseline is overstated: stage_mcp_tool_defs builds the mcp_catalog/mcp_call definitions (threshold 40, ceiling 200), but tool_loop.rs returns an error for both names and every mcp__ call, execution-core has no mcp_call handler, and trusted_capability_id returns None for dynamic MCP names so the signed gate fails closed, so registered MCP tools cannot run. Present: tool-result handles with result_query (inline loop), argument validation in both loops, process_* background processes and the Watch primitive with a process-output adapter. Absent: a deferred index over built-in tools, per-tool output schemas (ToolDefinition has only parameters_json), code mode (greenfield, no tool-RPC bridge), an agent-side wake on job completion, and WebMCP.

constraints: Both loops refuse MCP execution by design until capability-core provides a durable per-tool binding (F-t3-003), so a deferred index over MCP tools cannot ship first. The decision ledger records that offered_tool_defs() is the purpose-lock allowlist: hiding a tool from the rendered set forbids it, so a deferred index first needs the allowlist decoupled from the rendered set. Code mode must route every sub-call through EvaluatePolicy and approvals, keep the sandbox network-off except the bridge, and keep intermediate data out of persisted history under ZDR. WebMCP page tools must be proposed by the Model and executed or rejected by Quarry, never by a Model Plane browser.
approachAdjustment: Reorder: (1) MCP enablement via F-t3-003 is the prerequisite, not "shipped"; (2) deferred index only after decoupling the purpose-lock allowlist, starting with description and schema budgeting with degrade-before-drop as the ledger advises; (3) typed outputs as an optional output schema on ToolDefinition, building on result handles; (4) code mode as its own XL item on top of F-t3-009, read-only tools first; (5) agent wake on process completion on the existing Watch primitive; (6) WebMCP last and optional.
effortNote: Raised from L because the bundle includes greenfield code mode and an MCP execution path that does not run yet; the deferred index and typed outputs alone would be M to L.
verdictReason: The item is correctly partial and correctly sequenced late, but its premise that MCP staged disclosure is shipped is wrong (definitions only, execution blocked), the purpose-lock constraint is missing, and process_* plus Watch already cover part of the background-job idea.
